details.content: Normalized probability q_n(w) is defined for each class n and word w.
F(w) is the fraction of documents that contains word w.
Prior Inhomogeneity of a set of documents is measured before using word w.
Inhomogeneity after using w is measured after applying word w to the document set.
New Gini-index of w is a metric used to evaluate the impurity of word w with respect to class distribution.
Information Gain quantifies the reduction in uncertainty about class labels after observing word w.
Mutual Information measures how a word w and a class n are correlated.
Expected co-occurrence of w and class n is P_n · F(w).
True co-occurrence of w and class n is p_n(w) · F(w).
M_n(w) = 0 indicates that word w is not relevant to class n.
M_n(w) > 0 indicates that word w is positively correlated to class n.
M_n(w) < 0 indicates that word w is negatively correlated to class n.
Average and maximum values of M_n(w) summarize the overall relevance of word w across classes.
p_n(w) may be biased when the global class distribution of documents is usually not uniform.
t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE) is an unsupervised, non-linear technique.
t-SNE is primarily used for data exploration and visualizing high-dimensional data.
t-SNE gives an intuition of how data is arranged in high dimensional space.
